scope: Exact DriftWM user-visible behavior for native Mac apps. User explicitly excluded Wayland/X11 client hosting; native behavior equivalents remain required.
coverage_note: Source-indexed inventory, not a complete semantic oracle. Includes commented reference defaults/examples and typed configuration fields. Source-dispatch contracts and production E2E remain required; example assignments are not automatically runtime defaults.

rows.contract: Match Action::Exec dispatch, parameters, context, repeat/fullscreen policy and errors.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E, including defaults, failure cases and lifecycle; record actual native effects where applicable.
rows.implementation_note: The controller action exec <cmd> runs nothing itself: it returns an exec effect carrying the command and the config's child environment, and the shell runs /bin/sh -c <cmd> with posix_spawn, detached in a session of its own with standard input and output on /dev/null, never waiting on the main loop. Reachable from a key or mouse binding in the config file and as msg action exec <cmd> over the IPC socket; fixture modes ignore the effect. Known mismatches: upstream's five Wayland toolkit environment fallbacks are withheld unless the file's [env] sets them; the shell adds INFINIFY_SOCKET (the socket it serves) where upstream's child_env carries WAYLAND_DISPLAY, unless [env] sets it; the cursor is not revealed; any same-user process that can write to the socket can have the app run a command, as with upstream's msg action exec. No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is limited to exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios (the effect, not the process), and one scripted msg session against the built app in --windowed mode, in which an exec'd command wrote its environment to a file, left no saved evidence; a key or mouse binding firing it is unrun on a live run. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

Known mismatches: upstream probes a list of Linux terminals and falls back to foot, none of which exists on macOS, so the fallback is a macOS substitute rather than upstream's list. rows.implementation_note: The controller action spawn <cmd> returns the same exec effect as exec <cmd>, which the shell runs as /bin/sh -c <cmd>, detached. Unlike exec it is repeatable, as upstream: a hot key bound to it fires again while held, after input.keyboard.repeat_delay and then repeat_rate times a second. Reachable from a key or mouse binding in the config file and as msg action spawn <cmd>. Known mismatches: as for exec (Wayland toolkit environment fallbacks withheld, no cursor reveal, the socket lets a same-user process run a command); upstream's default spawn bindings (swaylock, wpctl, brightnessctl, playerctl, grim) name Linux programs that sh will not find on a Mac, and those on media keys are not registered at all. No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is limited to exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios (the effect, not the process), and one scripted msg session against the built app in --windowed mode, in which spawn touch <file> created the file, left no saved evidence; a key binding firing it and its repeat are unrun on a live run. rows.contract: Match Action::CloseWindow dispatch, parameters, context, repeat/fullscreen policy and errors.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E, including defaults, failure cases and lifecycle; record actual native effects where applicable.
rows.implementation_note: The controller action close-window acts on the focused window. For a window with a bound source it returns a close_window effect naming that binding (window, identity, generation) and marks the close as real, so session.suspend_on_close leaves no stand-in when window_closed later reports the window gone; nothing is removed until then. A focused detached placeholder (stand-in or waiting slot) is dismissed, with upstream's focus-follow. With no focused window nothing happens. Default shell: Control-Option-Q (upstream mod+q) and msg action close-window; the shell performs the effect only from an action or IPC reply, by pressing that window's own close button through Accessibility after validating process id, process birth and window number afresh, and only when Accessibility access exists. The mark lapses after upstream's 10 seconds. Known mismatches: those 10 seconds are measured on the navigation clock the host ticks (the app's shell ticks it every 80 ms while the canvas is open), not on a wall clock, and a press the shell skipped is not reported back, so its mark simply lapses; the focused window is the canvas's logical focus, which follows native focus only where native focus is allowed (Accessibility access, and no --no-native-focus); an Accessibility press that is not answered in time is treated as sent; no fullscreen or modal policy (with a widget focused it does nothing). No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios only (crates/desktop/tests/lifecycle_flow.rs); the scripted msg launches of the built app on 2026-10-09 had neither Screen Recording nor Accessibility access, reached placeholders only and left no saved evidence: a focused placeholder was dismissed there, and the close button press and the hot key are unrun. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.contract: Match Action::SuspendWindow dispatch, parameters, context, repeat/fullscreen policy and errors.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E, including defaults, failure cases and lifecycle; record actual native effects where applicable.
rows.implementation_note: The controller action suspend-window acts on the focused window. For a window with a bound source it marks the window for suspension and returns the same close_window effect as close-window; when window_closed reports the window gone, a stand-in (a detached placeholder keeping the logical id, world frame and stacking, listed in the scene file's standins) takes its place. A window without a bundle identifier could not be relaunched and is closed for real instead. A focused placeholder is dismissed, upstream's second press. Default shell: msg action suspend-window or a config binding (upstream binds no default key); the effect is performed as for close-window. Known mismatches: the window is not converted at once, the stand-in appears only when the native window has gone, so an application that refuses to close keeps its live window; the suspend mark lapses after upstream's 10 seconds, measured on the navigation clock the host ticks rather than a wall clock, so an application that takes longer to close leaves what suspend_on_close says; the stand-in keeps the window's current world frame, not the frame at the moment of the action; a stand-in is drawn like any detached placeholder, without upstream's name label and without click or Enter relaunch; no dialog exclusion. No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios only (crates/desktop/tests/lifecycle_flow.rs); the scripted msg launches of the built app on 2026-10-09 had neither Screen Recording nor Accessibility access, reached placeholders only and left no saved evidence: a focused stand-in was dismissed there, and the suspension of a live window is unrun. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.contract: Match Action::NudgeWindow dispatch, parameters, context, repeat/fullscreen policy and errors.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E, including defaults, failure cases and lifecycle; record actual native effects where applicable.
rows.implementation_note: The controller action nudge-window <dir> moves the focused logical window by navigation.nudge_step world points along the direction's unit vector, each axis rounded as upstream rounds it; with no focused window, or with a widget or a screen-pinned window focused, nothing happens and nothing is saved. It is a logical world move through the same path as the IPC Move: refused during a drag or resize gesture, during a live native resize of that window, and for a destination outside the 32-bit range. Default shell: Control-Option-Shift with an arrow key (upstream mod+shift+arrow), repeating while held; also msg action nudge-window <dir>. Known mismatches: the native window is never moved; the frame jumps at once where upstream animates it from its old place; the window is not raised. It ends a fill restore point as upstream's does; one can exist only for a window filled behind --experimental-native-resize, never in a default launch. No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is limited to exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios, and one scripted msg session against the built app in --windowed mode, in which a focused placeholder moved by the configured step, left no saved evidence; the hot key and its repeat are unrun on a live run. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.contract: Match Action::GrowWindow dispatch, parameters, context, repeat/fullscreen policy and errors.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E, including defaults, failure cases and lifecycle; record actual native effects where applicable.
rows.implementation_note: Status stays missing: the policy exists only behind --experimental-native-resize. With the flag the shell sends native_resize_capability and grow-window <dir> follows upstream's step_resize_focused: the focused window's named edge moves outward by navigation.resize_step (a diagonal moves both of its edges by the rounded share of the step) and the opposite edge stays where it is for whatever size the window grants; with a widget or a screen-pinned window focused nothing happens, as upstream's is_canvas_window filter leaves it. The action begins the existing size-only native resize transaction without a drag, and the size the window is then observed to have is committed and anchored; a repeat that arrives while a size is still owed walks on from the size asked for, and a drag of the window is refused until the size has arrived. Without the flag the action answers action not implemented on macOS yet: grow-window, byte for byte as before, and a key bound to it is not registered. Unbound by default, as upstream. Known mismatches: the frame changes when the native result arrives, not at the request; native size limits are unknown, so only upstream's one-pixel floor is applied before asking; there is one size transaction, so a step on other edges or on another window while one is pending is refused instead of applied; a stand-in is refused (grow-window needs a live window: a stand-in has no native size to change) where upstream resizes its frame; during a pointer drag it is refused where upstream bails silently. No evidence entry is recorded: coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios in which the test plays the native side (crates/desktop/tests/sizes_flow.rs), and scripted msg sessions against the built app on 2026-10-10 that reached only the not-implemented reply without the flag and the stand-in refusal with it. No native window was resized. What remains: a live native resize pass on a real window.

rows.implementation_note: Status stays missing: the policy exists only behind --experimental-native-resize. With the flag shrink-window <dir> is Action.GrowWindow with a negative step: the focused window's named edge moves inward by navigation.resize_step, down to upstream's one-pixel floor, and the opposite edge stays where it is for whatever size the window grants, through the same size-only native resize transaction begun without a drag. rows.implementation_note: center-window runs through the action command in every normal launch: it ends a cycle in progress, then focuses and flies to the focused canvas window, or with none, or with a widget or a screen-pinned window focused, to the canvas window whose centre is nearest the viewport centre (detached placeholders included; no widget and no pinned window, as upstream's is_canvas_window), at zoom 1. Default shell: toolbar Center and the config file's binding (upstream's default mod+c, Control-Option-C under the default super chord). Known mismatches: upstream's RestoreFillElseReset returns to the fill's camera and zoom only for a window filled behind --experimental-native-resize and is Reset in every default launch, where no fill can exist; fullscreen and modal handling are absent; the native focus request it returns is performed only with Accessibility access and has never been exercised live. No evidence entry is recorded for this change: coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios (crates/desktop/tests/navigation_actions_flow.rs, expected targets derived by hand, not from an executed upstream oracle), the headless coordinator regression (tests/e2e/desktop-navigation.sh) and scripted msg sessions against the built app in --windowed mode on 2026-10-09 with detached placeholders only (with a focused window, after focus --id, and with focus cleared), which left no saved evidence. The toolbar button, hot-key delivery and native focus are unrun on a live run. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.contract: Match Action::CenterNearest dispatch, parameters, context, repeat/fullscreen policy and errors.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E, including defaults, failure cases and lifecycle; record actual native effects where applicable.
rows.implementation_note: center-nearest <direction> runs through the action command in every normal launch, with driftwm-core's find_nearest and upstream's closest-point rule: candidates are every canvas window (detached placeholders included; no widget and no screen-pinned window) and the navigation.anchors points; the search starts at the focused window while all of it is on the output (upstream's threshold 1.0) and it is not screen-pinned, and at the viewport centre otherwise; a window is focused and flown to at the current zoom (NavZoom::Keep), and an anchor clears focus and flies the camera there. Default shell: the config file's bindings (upstream's default mod+arrows, Control-Option-arrows under the default super chord). Known mismatches: representative points come from the world rectangle, which has no separate title-bar strip; a fractional frame's visibility is measured by the largest whole-pixel rectangle inside it; there is no just-exited-fullscreen anchor; an anchor outside the ±1e12 world is not a candidate; the gesture form (ThresholdAction.CenterNearest) has run only as a synthetic event stream, and the pointer form has its own row (MouseAction.CenterNearest); the native focus request is performed only with Accessibility access and has never been exercised live. No evidence entry is recorded yet: coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios (crates/desktop/tests/navigation_actions_flow.rs, expected targets derived by hand, not from an executed upstream oracle) and scripted msg sessions against the built app in --windowed mode on 2026-10-09 with detached placeholders only (right, left, up, down and up-right, a kept zoom, the viewport-centre origin, an anchor), which left no saved evidence. Hot-key delivery and native focus are unrun on a live run. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.implementation_note: cycle-windows forward|backward runs through the action command in every normal launch: one step through the frozen focus history from upstream's cycle anchor (the logical focus), flown to at the current zoom. A fire with a real modifier physically down keeps the cycle open, and the shell ends it when the cycle_hold modifiers are no longer all down, by sampling the session's modifier state 60 times a second; a modifier-less fire (toolbar Previous and Next, IPC) is a single committed step; any other action ends the cycle first. Default shell: upstream's default alt+Tab and alt+shift+Tab as Option-Tab and Option-Shift-Tab hot keys from the config, replacing the former hard-coded ones, and toolbar Previous and Next. Known mismatches: with native focus allowed the focus history is promoted only by confirmed or observed native focus, so a selection whose focus request fails, or is superseded before it is confirmed, is not promoted where upstream would promote it; without Accessibility access or with --no-native-focus the shell answers every focus request focus_logical and the history follows logical focus instead, as upstream's follows keyboard focus; every canvas press ends an open cycle at the press, committing a settled selection, where upstream ends it only when another window takes focus or the hold modifiers are let go; an IPC cycle-windows is a single step even with a modifier down; a widget and a screen-pinned window never enter the history, and a step taken from one starts at its head, as upstream; modal and fullscreen policies are absent. No evidence entry is recorded for this change: coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios (crates/desktop/tests/navigation_actions_flow.rs, focus_cycle_flow.rs) and the headless coordinator regression (tests/e2e/desktop-navigation.sh, injected driver and modifier readings); in scripted msg sessions against the built app on 2026-10-09 the action replied Ok and changed nothing, because the scene held detached placeholders only and they never enter the history. A cycle that changes the order in the running app, the hot keys, the Option release and native focus are unrun on a live run. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.implementation_note: Camera-only controller go-to-bookmark <name>, parsed by the upstream action grammar, animates the output's camera so its usable-area centre lands on the stored canvas point, leaves zoom untouched and clears the output's Fit return. Bookmarks are the controller's own name -> [x, y] registry of centre points, Y up, seeded from the config's [navigation.bookmarks] (upstream's four corner seeds 1 to 4 when the file has no such table) and read back from the scene file only with session.restore_bookmarks = true; they are separate from the canvas Scene's camera-and-zoom bookmark map. Default shell: the config file's bindings of go-to-bookmark <name> (upstream's defaults mod+1 to mod+4, Control-Option-1 to 4 under the default super chord), with a status-line hint when the bookmark does not exist; also reachable as msg action go-to-bookmark <name>. Known mismatches: no fullscreen interaction (Infinify has no fullscreen yet). No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is limited to exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios, and shortcut delivery, the Unix-socket path and rendered animation are unverified on a live run. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.contract: Match Action::SetBookmark dispatch, parameters, context, repeat/fullscreen policy and errors.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E, including defaults, failure cases and lifecycle; record actual native effects where applicable.
rows.implementation_note: Camera-only controller set-bookmark <name> stores, as a centre point with Y up, the canvas point under the output's usable-area centre, computed as upstream does from the pending camera target, else the camera, and the current zoom: that is the destination of a camera-only flight (pan-viewport, go-to-bookmark, an IPC camera write), but an anchored zoom flight (home toggle, zoom step, fit, their returns, an IPC zoom write, window navigation) drops its camera target on its first tick, so a bookmark set during one captures the point under the usable-area centre at that moment (before that tick, the camera target paired with the zoom not yet changed), which is the flight's destination only by coincidence. It replaces any bookmark of that name in the live registry and reports the scene dirty; zoom is never stored. The registry is written to the scene file only with session.restore_bookmarks = true: with upstream's default (false) a bookmark set at runtime lasts until quit, and a save carries the file's earlier bookmarks forward untouched. Default shell: the config file's bindings of set-bookmark <name> (upstream's defaults mod+shift+1 to mod+shift+4, Control-Option-Shift-1 to 4 under the default super chord) with a Bookmark saved status line; also reachable as msg action set-bookmark <name> and msg bookmark <name> <x> <y>. Known mismatches: a scene file that contains bookmarks cannot be read by older builds. No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is limited to exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios, and shortcut delivery, the Unix-socket path and a live scene save are unverified. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.implementation_note: Camera-only controller zoom-to-fit-snapped is zoom-to-fit over the focused canvas window's snap cluster only (driftwm-core's cluster_of with snap.gap), detached placeholders included and no widget or screen-pinned window in it, with zoom.fit_padding and the same toggle: the first press saves the output's camera and zoom as its Fit return and animates to frame the cluster, the next press animates back, and with no focused window, or with a widget or a screen-pinned window focused, and no return pending nothing happens. rows.contract: Match HotCorner::TopLeft dispatch, parameters, context, repeat/fullscreen policy and errors.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E, including defaults, failure cases and lifecycle; record actual native effects where applicable.
rows.implementation_note: An [[outputs]] hot_corners entry binds an action to the top-left corner of the output whose stable id (a display UUID, or windowed) equals the entry's name, or of every output without an entry of its own for name = "*"; the bindings command reports the bound corners of each registered output. While some corner is bound the shell reads the pointer and runs upstream's check_hot_corners latch: the action fires once when the pointer comes within threshold points of both edges of the corner, is armed again when the pointer leaves, and under disable_while_dragging an entry made while a mouse button is held or a gesture runs is latched without firing. The controller's hot_corner command then runs the bound action through the normal action dispatch with that output active. Normal runs only. Known mismatches: the pointer is sampled every 80 ms (60 times a second during a camera flight) instead of on every motion, so a pass through the corner between two samples is missed; the corner is measured on the display's panel, the toolbar strip included, not on the output; disable_when_fullscreen suppresses the corner only behind --experimental-native-resize, where a window can be fullscreen, and has nothing to suppress in a default launch (see config.outputs.hot_corners.disable_when_fullscreen). No evidence entry is recorded yet: the controller side is covered by exported-C-ABI/JSON scenarios (crates/desktop/tests/platform_actions_flow.rs); the shell's latch was run only in its author's scratch harness, and no corner has been fired on a live run (a launch of the built app with top_left bound loaded its config cleanly, and no pointer was moved into the corner). Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.contract: Match wire format, CLI grammar, selectors, coordinates, reply semantics, errors and subscriptions for Request::State.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E, including defaults, failure cases and lifecycle; record actual native effects where applicable.
rows.implementation_note: Returns upstream's StateInfo shape. Camera and zoom are the centre of the request output's whole view (its screen_bounds size, not the usable area; Y up) and its zoom, and each output's camera is the same centre of that output. Each window carries id (Infinify's logical window id), app_id (the bundle identifier), title, position (the world rect's centre, Y up, rounded to integers), size, is_focused, is_widget (from the window's rule), suspended (the window has no bound source, so a detached placeholder is Infinify's stand-in) and mode (always Normal). Outputs carry name (the output's stable id), camera, zoom, size and active (the request's output, supplied by the shell); active_bookmark comes from the canvas policy crate's active-bookmark helper with a per-output incumbent kept as ephemeral state. No evidence entry is recorded: coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios in which the test plays the native side (crates/desktop/tests/rules_flow.rs); no rule was resolved in a running app and no native window was resized. rows.implementation_note: A matching rule's pass_keys (true, or a list of key combos, parsed and merged by driftwm-core's own code) is asked of the config and the window's title of the moment, as upstream's live_rule_for asks it. The controller reports in every snapshot what the window that holds the keyboard passes (null, true, or the combos spelled as the bindings reply spells a key binding's combo) and marks each key binding passable; the shell compares that at each redraw and, when it changed, unregisters the Carbon hot keys of the passed, passable bindings, so that macOS itself delivers the chord to the frontmost application, and registers them again when the focus leaves. Nothing is posted or injected. A stand-in and a detached slot pass nothing, as upstream skips a suspended window. Known mismatches: the decision is made per focus change, not per key press, and a window's rule counts only once its native focus is confirmed or observed (or the request is answered focus_logical), so nothing is passed while a focus request for a window other than the one last observed natively is in flight or after such a request failed (a request for the window the last native observation names leaves that window's value standing, in flight and failed alike: it still holds the keyboard); a key held when its binding becomes passed stays a binding until its release; the binding on the shell's exit chord and every quit binding are never passed, in the place of upstream's VT switch, where upstream passes its quit binding; a list matches a binding by its combo text, so of two upstream combos on one physical chord (mod+q and ctrl+alt+q under the default super chord) only the one holding the chord passes; with --no-native-focus or without Accessibility the released chords go to whichever application is frontmost; media keys are not registered by the shell, so nothing changes for them; a --windowed run registers no hot keys. No evidence entry is recorded yet: coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios only (crates/desktop/tests/passthrough_flow.rs); the shell's hot key code was compiled and read only, and in the one launch of the built app on 2026-10-10 (windowed, no Screen Recording access, placeholders only) no key was pressed, no hot key was seen being unregistered and no real window received a passed key. rows.implementation_note: A matching rule's pass_mouse (true, or a list of mouse combos, parsed and merged by driftwm-core's own code) is asked of the config and the window's title of the moment. The shell names the window under the pointer in its mouse_binding lookup for a button press and for a wheel or trackpad scroll; once a binding has matched in the window context, upstream's claim (pass_mouse_claims through PassList::allows; the subject is the window under the pointer, the pinned one first, then the topmost, never the focused one) answers binding null with passed true, and the shell treats the trigger as unbound: a press focuses the window and is forwarded to it, a scroll is forwarded, by the existing forward path. For each event of a discrete wheel the shell asks the wheel-notch lookup first (wheel_up, wheel_down), where upstream's notch site sits: a notch bound to an action runs it and consumes the event, and an unbound or passed notch goes on to the continuous scroll lookup, so a claim on mod+wheel-up leaves a mod+wheel-scroll zoom firing. Below zoom.interact_min upstream's pick-mode gate applies: a canvas window, a pick target there (the lookup's pick argument), claims nothing, and a screen-pinned window keeps its button claims and loses its scroll and notch claims while its own output is below the threshold. A stand-in and a detached slot claim nothing, nothing is claimed on empty canvas or during the 150 ms canvas lock after a finger pan, and trackpad gestures ask no claim, as upstream's dispatch asks none. Known mismatches: a widget that is not pinned keeps its claims below zoom.interact_min, where upstream's button and scroll sites drop them, because the lookup is told the window and whether it is a pick target but not the pointer's output; one wheel line counts as one notch, with no accumulator for a high-resolution wheel; upstream's fullscreen leg, a fullscreen window's claims with no pick gate, holds for the window hit reports on a fullscreen output, which exists only behind --experimental-native-resize, and not in the band a smaller fullscreen window leaves (navigation.fullscreen); a claim is asked about the one upstream combo the binding matched under; no compositor chrome exists on a live window for upstream's rule that chrome is never pass_mouse's to give (hit tests the frame only). No evidence entry is recorded yet: coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios only (crates/desktop/tests/passthrough_flow.rs, upstream's src/tests/pass_mouse.rs restated as lookups); the shell's hooks and its notch site were compiled and read only, and in the launches of the built app on 2026-10-10 (windowed, no Screen Recording access, placeholders only) no press or scroll was made, no wheel was turned and no real window received a passed one. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E, including defaults, failure cases and lifecycle; record actual native effects where applicable.
rows.implementation_note: [effects] blur_radius, the number of blur passes behind a blurred window, is reported as render.effects.blur_radius exactly as driftwm-core's parse_effects_config leaves it (default 2; a negative or non-integer value is a parse failure that refuses the file) and reaches the shell's compositor as frame.effects on the render revision every accepted reload spends. The compositor is the Metal port of upstream's dual Kawase blur (native/desktop/COMPOSITOR-NOTES.md, Part II), which frosts what lies beneath a window whose decoration.blur is set. Known mismatches: a capture holds no frost, as upstream's screenshot composer omits it; probe, demo and owned-fixture runs draw none; see field.Config.effects. No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios only (crates/desktop/tests/effects_flow.rs, against driftwm-core's own parse of the same text); on 2026-10-10 a reload to 4 was seen to reach the renderer's frame, and a frost was drawn with it, in frames a throwaway tool outside the repository read back from the shell's renderer driven by this controller's snapshots, under a synthetic plain-coloured buffer at opacity 0.6 over a stand-in; the picture at one radius was not compared with another, and in the built app, which had no Screen Recording access and whose panel nobody looked at, nothing of it was seen (msg cannot read render.effects). Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.contract: Match EffectsConfig.animation_speed type, validation, default and live effect.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E, including defaults, failure cases and lifecycle; record actual native effects where applicable.
rows.implementation_note: [effects] animation_speed is reported as render.effects.animation_speed as driftwm-core's parser leaves it (default 0.5; 0, a negative value or nan is the default and a value above 1 is 1, each with upstream's warning) and is the lerp factor per 60 Hz frame of the animations the shell's compositor plays from the snapshot's lifecycle_events, each event once: upstream's open scale and fade when a window maps after the launch pass (open), its closing snapshot when one closes (close, and alpha only over the stand-in for close_to_standin), and its two stand-in fades (standin_dismiss, standin_adopted). At 1 nothing is played, as upstream's animations end on their first tick. The existing frame timer runs while one is in progress and stops afterwards. Known mismatches: upstream's move, resize, fit and fullscreen animations, which the key also drives, do not exist here; the windows of the launch pass and a window that takes its own waiting slot back animate nothing (the macOS adoption rule); an opening window, and the stand-in a relaunched window adopted, wait for the window's first stream picture, a second at most, where upstream starts at the first sized commit; a ctrl-option-click removes a placeholder through forget, which upstream has not: it logs standin_dismiss with no output, so the placeholder fades as a dismissed stand-in does, without upstream's focus rules; under --experimental-native-resize a window that opens while a rule's size is owed waits for that size transaction as well, ten seconds at most, and a window whose picture is withheld when it closes fades from nothing; each output bakes its own closing snapshot where upstream shares one, and upstream's one-second age limit on a closing window's pixels has no separate test; probe, demo and owned-fixture runs animate nothing. No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios only (crates/desktop/tests/effects_flow.rs: the value against driftwm-core's parse, and which commands log which event); on 2026-10-10, in frames two throwaway tools outside the repository read back from the shell's renderer, an open, a close, a close into a stand-in, an adoption crossfade and a dismissal logged by this controller each played once and ended after 0.68 to 0.71 s at a configured 0.1 (upstream's length there is 0.73 s), the first frame at the default was half way, and a hand-written speed of 1 played nothing; every picture was a synthetic plain-coloured buffer or a stand-in, the loop standing in for the frame timer ticked about every 25 ms, and in the built app, which had no Screen Recording access and whose panel nobody looked at, two stand-ins were dismissed over msg with nothing seen of the fade. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.implementation_note: Part of every window's decoration in the snapshot, resolved by driftwm-core's effective_* helpers and drawn as upstream draws it: border_width is a ring outside the content in border_color, or in border_color_focused on the window with the controller's logical focus; corner_radius clips the content and shapes the ring and the shadow; shadow is upstream's 14-unit shadow; opacity and opacity_focused multiply every pass of a window that neither a rule nor msg opacity pins. A frame that exactly covers the output loses radius and shadow, and the border too when it overhangs (upstream's DrawnChrome). A stand-in takes its border, radius and shadow from this table alone and is always opaque, as upstream's: opacity and opacity_focused never dim one. Known mismatches: see render.chrome. No evidence entry is recorded yet: seen only in PNGs msg screenshot wrote from the built app on 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10, on stand-ins, at the defaults and at one other value each, opacity and opacity_focused excepted: a stand-in stayed at alpha 255 under opacity = 0.5, so no opacity was ever seen applied. No captured window ever wore any of it. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.implementation_note: [decorations] opacity is what a window that does not hold the canvas's logical focus is drawn at when it has no opacity of its own from a rule or an IPC write, through driftwm-core's own effective_opacity; a widget stays at 1. Each placement reports it as opacity and as decoration.opacity, one function's answer, and the shell's compositor multiplies every pass of the window by it; a reload of the key changes both and spends a render revision. Known mismatches: focus is the canvas's logical focus, not native keyboard focus; the picture on the canvas fades, not the application's own window on the desktop; probe, demo and owned-fixture runs fade a layer tile instead; see render.chrome. rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E, including defaults, failure cases and lifecycle; record actual native effects where applicable.
rows.implementation_note: [decorations] blur (default false) makes decoration.blur true for every window with a bound source, a widget and a screen-pinned window included, through driftwm-core's own effective_blur over the rule the window mapped with; a reload of the key changes it for the windows already there and spends a render revision. A stand-in and a waiting slot are never blurred, as upstream requests blur for client windows only. The shell sets the flag on the window's element and the compositor frosts what lies beneath it at full strength, which shows where the window is translucent (an opacity below 1, or content with alpha). Known mismatches: upstream's exemption of a fullscreen window applies only where a window can be fullscreen, behind --experimental-native-resize (navigation.fullscreen); a capture holds no frost, as upstream's; probe, demo and owned-fixture runs draw none; see field.EffectsConfig.blur_radius. No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios only (crates/desktop/tests/effects_flow.rs, against driftwm-core's effective_blur); on 2026-10-10, in frames a throwaway tool outside the repository read back from the shell's renderer driven by this controller's snapshots, a controller-placed window on a synthetic red buffer reported blur true under blur = true and was drawn at opacity 0.6 with the stand-in's label behind it blurred, while the stand-ins reported false; in the built app, which had no Screen Recording access and so no bound window, viewport captures with the key on were byte-identical to those with it off and nothing else was seen. Whether a captured Mac window's own translucency lets a frost through is unknown. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.implementation_note: Default shell, normal runs only: canvas views accept indirect trackpad touches, and a recogniser (native/desktop/trackpad-gestures.m) turns three or more fingers into libinput-shaped swipe, pinch and hold streams, a three-finger tap marking the next swipe as a doubletap; a two-finger pinch is AppKit's magnify stream sent the same way. The controller dispatches them against the [gestures] tables as upstream's src/input/gestures does, by trigger, finger count, modifiers and window-or-canvas context, and a gesture ends cancelled when the finger count changes, the system takes the touches, a button is pressed or the trackpad is turned off. Known mismatches: this path has never received a touch. The recogniser's rules and constants imitate libinput from its documentation and from memory, were not checked against its source and were not tuned; whether macOS delivers three- and four-finger touches to the non-activating canvas panel, and every finger in every event, is unknown; macOS's own three- and four-finger gestures must be turned off by the user in System Settings (nothing here changes a setting), and coexistence with them is untested; six default bindings name actions that do not run in a default launch (fit-window, fit-window-snapped, toggle-fullscreen; all three run behind --experimental-native-resize) and the resize gestures are gated; an unbound gesture is not forwarded to the application under the pointer, so source-app gesture and focus coexistence is absent; two-finger scrolling stays a mouse binding. No evidence entry is recorded yet: the dispatch is covered by exported-C-ABI/JSON scenarios with synthetic event streams (crates/desktop/tests/gesture_flow.rs) and the recogniser by scripted touch sequences in throwaway programs, while the app's touch, timer and magnify glue is compiled and reviewed only. No physical trackpad gesture has been performed. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.implementation_note: Normal-window anchor/zoom animation is integrated through one controller frame clock at21b454d. Scroll momentum now runs on the same clock: a timed pan feeds upstream's own MomentumState (driftwm-core) per output, pan_end launches it, a trackpad gesture's swipe pan and its end are that pan and that pan_end, and each tick runs scroll momentum, edge pan, zoom and camera in upstream's order, with momentum stopped where upstream stops it (a flight target or anchor, the action prelude, a press, a grab install, a bound swipe or pinch). The shell times pans from their events, sends pan_end at the scroll phase's end, on release and 50 ms after the last pan, and drops macOS's own inertia for canvas pans. A scroll under a held drag pan leaves its launch to the release, and a scroll that a window takes over part-way is forwarded from there with its end and inertia. Momentum is covered by exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios (crates/desktop/tests/motion_flow.rs, bit for bit against MomentumState, and crates/desktop/tests/gesture_flow.rs, a swipe's coast bit for bit against the same deltas sent as timed pans); no scroll, drag or swipe was made on a live run, so coasting, its timing against real events and native frame scheduling remain unverified, and broader camera actions remain unintegrated.

rows.contract: Edge zones/speeds, monitor-edge dwell and continuous move/resize behavior.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E, including defaults, failure cases and lifecycle; record actual native effects where applicable.
rows.implementation_note: Controller edge pan adapted from edge_pan.rs and the move grab's hook: during a window drag whose gesture_to carries the pointer, or one a move gesture drives with its virtual pointer, a pointer within navigation.edge_pan.zone of an edge of the drag's output arms a per-output request with upstream's ramp (speed_min at the zone's boundary to speed_max at the edge by squared depth, a corner cut back to the same length), and every frame pans the camera by that many screen points over the zoom and carries the dragged window or cluster by the same world delta, so it stays under the held pointer. A component that pushes at an edge shared with another output, found from the outputs' screen_bounds, waits edge_pan.latency_ms; an outer edge is immediate. Cursor edge pan arms the same request (see Action.ToggleCursorPan). The shell passes the pointer with every drag event and keeps its frame timer running while the controller reports the pan. Known mismatches: a drag stays on the output it began on, so nothing crosses to another output and there is no inhibited entry edge; the pointer is never warped; a resize gesture and touch drags arm no edge pan; only edge pan carries a dragged window, where upstream's grab follows every camera move; the velocity is per frame, so the speed is that of the shell's 60 Hz timer; fullscreen and lock stand-downs are absent. No evidence entry is recorded yet: coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios only (crates/desktop/tests/motion_flow.rs, and crates/desktop/tests/gesture_flow.rs for the move gesture, against values derived by hand from upstream's formulas, not by executing upstream); the shell side is compiled and reviewed only, because it needs a real window drag or move gesture, and no edge pan was produced on a live run. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.implementation_note: Status stays missing: the policy exists only behind --experimental-native-resize (see Action.ToggleFullscreen). With the flag the controller keeps one fullscreen window per output with what its exit restores (crates/desktop/src/fullscreen.rs, adapted from src/state/fullscreen.rs). Camera locking: the output is parked at its whole-pixel camera at zoom 1, no flight, momentum, edge pan or zoom-to-fit return is armed on it, and every command ends by putting it back there. What ends it is upstream's list: toggle-fullscreen, every action Action::runs_during_fullscreen does not list, IPC Camera and Zoom writes, IPC Suspend (IPC Close ends none, as upstream cmd_close), a bound pan, zoom or grab and a continuous trackpad gesture on that output, the native activation of another window there (a new window that macOS made key as it opened among them, where upstream keeps a background-placed window unfocused), the fullscreen window closing or losing its source, another window whose rule says fullscreen or a send-to-output taking the output, and the output's removal; a new window mapping does not itself end it and is placed in the background beside the saved frame (upstream's fullscreen_background_pos). Focus: the window is raised and focused on entering, stays in the focus history, is passed over by cycle-windows, is focused only on its own output, and with focus_follows_mouse a hover on its output gives it the focus back. Chrome and placement: a fullscreen output's snapshot has one placement, marked fullscreen, in global screen points at zoom 1 with a bare decoration (mode none, no border, radius or shadow) and upstream's effective_opacity and effective_blur with is_fullscreen; outputs[].fullscreen names the window and a black or canvas backdrop (upstream's fullscreen_conceals_canvas: canvas when the rule's or IPC opacity is below 1); hit, input and hover on that output reach only that window, and no other output places it. IPC State lists it under fullscreen and leaves it out of windows. The shell's renderer draws the marked placement at its screen rectangle at zoom 1 with the compositor's fullscreen decoration, clears to black or keeps the background and the outlines for the canvas backdrop, and draws no resize handle on it. Without the flag no output is ever fullscreen and outputs[].fullscreen is null. Known mismatches: no transition, and a placeholder while a size is unresolved; a size is committed only by a native observation, so after an exit the window keeps the output's size until its transaction answers, and after an exit made by pan, zoom, begin_drag, an output change or a displaced incumbent that transaction begins only with the next action, IPC, gesture, activate, clear_focus or pick reply, never with a hover's; a resize drag out of fullscreen starts from the output's size; output removal is settled at outputs_settled, not at remove_output; on the band beside a smaller fullscreen window only that window is hit, and mouse_binding names no output, so a press there resolves in the canvas context; the older cycle_focus command does not pass over a fullscreen window; a capture draws the canvas, not the fullscreen output; an exit whose transaction ended before the window was asked is begun again, three transactions at most; a window the adapter cannot resize enters with no transaction, centred; a window still fullscreen at Quit or Return to desktop is handed its size back by the shell before the save (compiled, run only with nothing fullscreen), and when that is cut off it is saved at its old place with the size it has, not upstream's frame from before; upstream's scenarios that need a Wayland surface (unacknowledged commits, pointer constraints, the frozen exit picture, a coasting camera) are not ported. Beside the milestones it was merged with: a grab ends the fullscreen, then raises and focuses the window, then takes hold, upstream's order for a press bound to move or resize; a fullscreen window claims by pass_mouse with no pick gate and passes its pass_keys while it holds the keyboard; a pinned drag is frozen while the pointer is over a fullscreen output; a rule's size is owed, not asked first, beside its fullscreen, and a ruled window waits out a fullscreen's transaction; a fit or a fill out of fullscreen measures the window by the size it is owed, not the output's; the shell draws the error bar on a fullscreen output, no closing snapshot and no stand-in fade there, and does not hold the opening of a window that maps fullscreen (compiled and read, never drawn). Notes on other rows that say there is no fullscreen describe a default launch. No evidence entry is recorded: coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios in which the test plays the native side (crates/desktop/tests/fullscreen_flow.rs, 20 scenarios on two outputs, five of them added when fullscreen was merged with effects, pass-through, the pinned drag and the polish pass), an offscreen read-back of the shell's renderer on hand-written snapshots by a throwaway program outside the repository, and scripted msg sessions against the built app on 2026-10-10 on detached placeholders, in which no fullscreen could be entered. No native window was resized or presented fullscreen. What remains: a live native resize pass on a real window.

rows.implementation_note: Partial. A stand-in is a detached placeholder that keeps a closed window's logical id, world frame and stacking; the scene file lists stand-ins in an additive standins key, by logical id only. A window becomes one when it closes under session.suspend_on_close, a matching window rule or a suspend mark, provided it has a bundle identifier; close-window and IPC Close mark a real close instead. Relaunch asks the shell to open the application by bundle identifier and the next window of that application adopts the slot, oldest pending relaunch first; dismissal removes a stand-in and passes the focus on. In place of upstream's session restore there is a macOS rule, because applications outlive Infinify: every window keeps a slot in the scene file, running windows are re-adopted by bundle identifier and title in a discovery pass at launch and whenever the canvas reopens, a slot whose titled window the pass names as existing off screen keeps waiting for it, and at adoption_complete the other unmatched slots are dropped unless session.restore_windows keeps them as stand-ins. Marks lapse after upstream's 10 seconds and a pending relaunch after its 30. Known mismatches: both are measured on the navigation clock the host ticks, not a wall clock; there is no activation token, so the identity match stays open for the whole 30 seconds instead of 5; matching a slot by title is a macOS addition and is greedy one window at a time, so a slot can go to a sibling window of the same application; no dialog exclusion and no parent or modal tiers; a stand-in is drawn like any detached placeholder, with no name label and no click or Enter relaunch; a relaunch of an application that is not installed answers Ok and is reported by the shell; a window that is off screen during a discovery pass keeps its slot only if it has a title and the slot has that exact title, otherwise the slot is dropped or made a stand-in and the window is placed afresh; while the launch config file is refused no slot is dropped or made a stand-in. rows.implementation_note: With focus_follows_mouse = true the controller's hover command, which the shell sends for pointer motion over a canvas panel while no button is down (at most once per 60 Hz frame), is upstream's maybe_hover_focus: the window under the pointer in the layered hit order (the windows pinned to the output, then the canvas windows, then the widgets), a detached placeholder (upstream's stand-in) included, takes logical focus without being raised and with no camera motion, a screen-pinned window before the canvas beneath it and outside the focus history; a widget is passed over, pinned or not, and its application still gets the motion; empty canvas keeps the focus; a window that already holds the focus intent is left alone; a drag or resize gesture (a move gesture's drag and a pick-mode press's included), a drag pan whose button is down and a native resize that has not drained stand for upstream's pointer grab, and a trackpad gesture between its begin and its end and a scroll pan whose momentum is yet to launch hold the pointer as well; a hover stops no flight and no coast. The focus request goes to the navigation coordinator like a click's (performed natively with Accessibility access, otherwise answered focus_logical), and a native focus report that only echoes it is recorded without a raise or a flight; a request that failed or was withdrawn unanswered stops counting as echoed 3 seconds after its hover, on the controller's tick clock. With false (the default) hover reports the hit and moves no focus. A config reload applies at the next hover. Known mismatches: an open focus cycle also blocks hover focus, where upstream's hover would end the cycle; a trackpad gesture and a scroll about to launch block it too, which are no pointer grab upstream; the focus history is promoted when the request is answered, not at the hover; the native request activates and raises the real window although the canvas does not restack; the echo rule has no upstream counterpart; there are no fullscreen or modal windows, layer surfaces or client resize margins for upstream's exclusions and redirections to apply to; the cursor does not change. No evidence entry is recorded yet: coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios (crates/desktop/tests/pointer_flow.rs, a pinned window and a widget under the pointer among them, synthetic identities and focus results, expected values derived by hand, not from an executed upstream oracle) and one scripted launch of the built app on 2026-10-10 in --windowed mode with detached placeholders only, where the setting loaded as true and was reloaded as false with nothing on stderr; msg exposes neither the setting nor hover, so no pointer motion, no hover in the app, no native focus change and no echo has been observed. reference_occurrences.source_assignment: auto_navigate_on_close = true  # on close, pan to the newly focused window if off-screen

rows.implementation_note: Read when a closed or dismissed window passes the focus on. On, upstream's default: a spatially related follower from the focus history, the one cycle-windows walks, which a shell without native focus fills by answering every request focus_logical (a window in the closed frame's snap cluster, or overlapping it) that is not wholly inside the usable area is focused and the camera of the active output flies to it at the current zoom. Off: such a window is not a candidate, and the focus goes to the most recent or nearest window still visible, or to nobody. Known mismatches: the follower gets logical focus and a native focus request, which the shell's navigation coordinator performs or answers focus_logical like every other and which has never been performed on a real window, and macOS itself activates a window of its own choosing after a close; a window whose focus request failed or was superseded before its answer is not in the history and is not preferred; no parent or modal tier and no layer-surface condition; the app registers no usable area, so the visibility test is against the whole view. No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios only (crates/desktop/tests/lifecycle_flow.rs); the scripted msg launches of the built app on 2026-10-09 had no Screen Recording access, so no bound window closed and no follow flight was seen. rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E for parameters/defaults, dispatch, errors and lifecycle; verify actual native effects when applicable.

reference_occurrences.source_assignment: interact_min = 0.0          # zoom (1.0 = 100%) below which a window is too

rows.implementation_note: zoom.interact_min is the zoom below which an output is in upstream's pick mode: a pure function of that output's live zoom (strictly below; 0, the default, is off; driftwm-core clamps the value to 0..1 with upstream's warning). hit, input and hover report a canvas window or placeholder under the pointer there as a pick target and snapshot.outputs[].pick the mode; a screen-pinned window and a widget are never one and keep their pointer input, a pinned window also where it lies over a target; input refuses a pick target and hover answers forward false, so no press, drag, scroll or motion can be forwarded to its application. The shell focuses and raises a target at a press with any button and swallows the press, unless a held-modifier binding claims it (upstream's try_pick_button rule, answered by mouse_binding with pick), starts a single-window move once a left press drags past the 5 point click slop, and at a left release within the slop on the same display sends pick: upstream's resolve_pick, a navigation to the window at zoom 1 that lands per focus_placement. A scroll with no window binding over a target is looked up again in the canvas context, and what is found there pans, with momentum, or zooms like any bound scroll; one with no binding there either goes nowhere. A window drag begun from a pick-mode press is a drag like any other, edge pan included. Trackpad gestures do not read pick mode, as upstream's gesture handlers do not: a move gesture over a target moves it. A config reload applies at once. Known mismatches: pick mode is per output, not the active output's; a filled window is returned to its fill view, when that view is at or above the threshold, only behind --experimental-native-resize, where fill-window runs, so in a default launch a pick always lands at zoom 1; there is no pointing-hand cursor over a target; there is no fullscreen window to exclude, and a widget that is not pinned keeps its pass_mouse claims below the threshold, where upstream drops them (field.WindowRule.pass_mouse; a pick target claims nothing and a screen-pinned window keeps its button claims, as upstream, and the move binding drags a pinned window in screen space below the threshold as above it); a placeholder has no chrome to bypass, and the shell's Control-Option-click dismissal of a placeholder becomes a pick in pick mode. No evidence entry is recorded yet: coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios (crates/desktop/tests/pointer_flow.rs: zoom 0.4 under a threshold of 0.5, at 0.5 and 0.6, the threshold off, a second output, a live reload, drags of a window and of a stand-in, picks landing under focus_placement top-left with an outer gap, and a pinned window over a target and a widget beside it, neither picked; expected values derived by hand, not from an executed upstream oracle) and one scripted launch of the built app on 2026-10-10 in --windowed mode with detached placeholders only, where interact_min = 0.5 loaded with nothing on stderr, eight zoom-out actions took msg zoom from 1 to 0.467 and zoom-reset back to 1, and -1 and 5 written to the file were reported with upstream's below-minimum and above-maximum warnings; msg does not expose pick mode, so the mode itself, a pick-mode press, drag, pick or scroll and the refusal of forwarded input have not been observed in the app. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.implementation_note: Upstream's default mouse binding, read by driftwm-core. An entry for the same combo in the same [mouse.*] table replaces it, and "none" removes it. reference_occurrences.source_assignment: swipe_threshold = 12.0        # px cumulative distance before directional swipe fires

rows.implementation_note: Parsed by driftwm-core, upstream's own config code; a threshold swipe fires once when the accumulated finger vector reaches it, and a reload applies to the next update. A value of the wrong type is refused by the TOML parser with the whole file, and the previous configuration stays. Known mismatches: the unit is the shell recogniser's stand-in for libinput's pointer units, a constant 10.5 for each millimetre of finger travel, so the default of 12 is a little over a millimetre after the swipe is recognised. No evidence entry is recorded yet: coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios with synthetic event streams (crates/desktop/tests/gesture_flow.rs), and one scripted msg session against the built app on 2026-10-09 that loaded a file setting it and saw a wrong-typed value refused, leaving no saved evidence. No physical trackpad gesture has been performed. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.implementation_note: Status stays missing: the key is parsed by upstream's own config code (default true) and reported per output by the bindings command, but it has something to suppress only behind --experimental-native-resize, where a window can be fullscreen (see navigation.fullscreen); in a default launch no output is ever fullscreen, so the key is not observable there. With the flag the controller's hot_corner command runs nothing and answers a reply with no navigation, no effects and dirty false for a corner of an output that has a fullscreen window while the key is true, runs the bound action when it is false, and another output's fullscreen suppresses nothing; the shell's latch applies the same rule before it sends the corner, recording the entry first as upstream's check_hot_corners does, so leaving fullscreen with the pointer resting in the corner fires nothing. Known mismatches: the shell reads the output's fullscreen from the last snapshot it drew, so it can be one draw behind the controller. No evidence entry is recorded: the controller side is covered by an exported-C-ABI/JSON scenario in which the test plays the native side (crates/desktop/tests/fullscreen_flow.rs); the shell's latch was run only in its author's throwaway harness on hand-written entries; no corner has been fired on a live run and no window has been fullscreen in the app. What remains: a live native resize pass on a real window.

rows.implementation_note: With focus_follows_mouse = true the controller's hover command, which the shell sends for pointer motion over a canvas panel while no button is down (at most once per 60 Hz frame), is upstream's maybe_hover_focus: the window under the pointer in the layered hit order (the windows pinned to the output, then the canvas windows, then the widgets), a detached placeholder (upstream's stand-in) included, takes logical focus without being raised and with no camera motion, a screen-pinned window before the canvas beneath it and outside the focus history; a widget is passed over, pinned or not, and its application still gets the motion; empty canvas keeps the focus; a window that already holds the focus intent is left alone; a drag or resize gesture (a move gesture's drag and a pick-mode press's included), a drag pan whose button is down and a native resize that has not drained stand for upstream's pointer grab, and a trackpad gesture between its begin and its end and a scroll pan whose momentum is yet to launch hold the pointer as well; a hover stops no flight and no coast. The focus request goes to the navigation coordinator like a click's (performed natively with Accessibility access, otherwise answered focus_logical), and a native focus report that only echoes it is recorded without a raise or a flight; a request that failed or was withdrawn unanswered stops counting as echoed 3 seconds after its hover, on the controller's tick clock. With false (the default) hover reports the hit and moves no focus. A config reload applies at the next hover. Known mismatches: an open focus cycle also blocks hover focus, where upstream's hover would end the cycle; a trackpad gesture and a scroll about to launch block it too, which are no pointer grab upstream; the focus history is promoted when the request is answered, not at the hover; the native request activates and raises the real window although the canvas does not restack; the echo rule has no upstream counterpart; there are no fullscreen or modal windows, layer surfaces or client resize margins for upstream's exclusions and redirections to apply to; the cursor does not change. No evidence entry is recorded yet: coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios (crates/desktop/tests/pointer_flow.rs, a pinned window and a widget under the pointer among them, synthetic identities and focus results, expected values derived by hand, not from an executed upstream oracle) and one scripted launch of the built app on 2026-10-10 in --windowed mode with detached placeholders only, where the setting loaded as true and was reloaded as false with nothing on stderr; msg exposes neither the setting nor hover, so no pointer motion, no hover in the app, no native focus change and no echo has been observed. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.implementation_note: zoom.interact_min is the zoom below which an output is in upstream's pick mode: a pure function of that output's live zoom (strictly below; 0, the default, is off; driftwm-core clamps the value to 0..1 with upstream's warning). hit, input and hover report a canvas window or placeholder under the pointer there as a pick target and snapshot.outputs[].pick the mode; a screen-pinned window and a widget are never one and keep their pointer input, a pinned window also where it lies over a target; input refuses a pick target and hover answers forward false, so no press, drag, scroll or motion can be forwarded to its application. The shell focuses and raises a target at a press with any button and swallows the press, unless a held-modifier binding claims it (upstream's try_pick_button rule, answered by mouse_binding with pick), starts a single-window move once a left press drags past the 5 point click slop, and at a left release within the slop on the same display sends pick: upstream's resolve_pick, a navigation to the window at zoom 1 that lands per focus_placement. A scroll with no window binding over a target is looked up again in the canvas context, and what is found there pans, with momentum, or zooms like any bound scroll; one with no binding there either goes nowhere. A window drag begun from a pick-mode press is a drag like any other, edge pan included. Trackpad gestures do not read pick mode, as upstream's gesture handlers do not: a move gesture over a target moves it. A config reload applies at once. Known mismatches: pick mode is per output, not the active output's; a filled window is returned to its fill view, when that view is at or above the threshold, only behind --experimental-native-resize, where fill-window runs, so in a default launch a pick always lands at zoom 1; there is no pointing-hand cursor over a target; there is no fullscreen window to exclude, and a widget that is not pinned keeps its pass_mouse claims below the threshold, where upstream drops them (field.WindowRule.pass_mouse; a pick target claims nothing and a screen-pinned window keeps its button claims, as upstream, and the move binding drags a pinned window in screen space below the threshold as above it); a placeholder has no chrome to bypass, and the shell's Control-Option-click dismissal of a placeholder becomes a pick in pick mode. No evidence entry is recorded yet: coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios (crates/desktop/tests/pointer_flow.rs: zoom 0.4 under a threshold of 0.5, at 0.5 and 0.6, the threshold off, a second output, a live reload, drags of a window and of a stand-in, picks landing under focus_placement top-left with an outer gap, and a pinned window over a target and a widget beside it, neither picked; expected values derived by hand, not from an executed upstream oracle) and one scripted launch of the built app on 2026-10-10 in --windowed mode with detached placeholders only, where interact_min = 0.5 loaded with nothing on stderr, eight zoom-out actions took msg zoom from 1 to 0.467 and zoom-reset back to 1, and -1 and 5 written to the file were reported with upstream's below-minimum and above-maximum warnings; msg does not expose pick mode, so the mode itself, a pick-mode press, drag, pick or scroll and the refusal of forwarded input have not been observed in the app. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.contract: Match Config.window_placement type, validation, default and native behavior.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E for parameters/defaults, dispatch, errors and lifecycle; verify actual native effects when applicable.
rows.implementation_note: Read from the loaded config each time a window appears by itself and adopts no saved slot: center (upstream's default), cursor or auto pick its world position as the WindowPlacement.Center, WindowPlacement.Cursor and WindowPlacement.Auto rows describe, and a reload applies to the next window. Known mismatches: those of the three variant rows (zero chrome, no usable area registered by the app, no parent, fullscreen or blank-slate tiers); a window rule's position comes first and its size is not applied in a default launch (behind --experimental-native-resize it is asked once the window is placed); windows adopted into a saved slot keep the slot's frame and are not placed at all. No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios only (crates/desktop/tests/lifecycle_flow.rs); the scripted msg launches of the built app on 2026-10-09 had no Screen Recording access, so no window was discovered or placed. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.implementation_note: The file's [env] entries are the environment of every exec effect: the shell overlays them on its own environment for the /bin/sh -c child. Known mismatches: upstream's five Wayland toolkit fallbacks (MOZ_ENABLE_WAYLAND, QT_QPA_PLATFORM, SDL_VIDEODRIVER, GDK_BACKEND, ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT) are withheld unless the file's own [env] sets them; where upstream's child_env adds WAYLAND_DISPLAY the shell adds INFINIFY_SOCKET, the socket it serves, and an [env] entry of that name wins. No evidence entry is recorded yet: coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios (crates/desktop/tests/config_flow.rs) and one scripted msg session against the built app in --windowed mode on 2026-10-09, which left no saved evidence. rows.contract: Match Config.mouse type, validation, default and native behavior.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E for parameters/defaults, dispatch, errors and lifecycle; verify actual native effects when applicable.
rows.implementation_note: The mouse binding tables ([mouse.on-window], [mouse.on-canvas], [mouse.anywhere]) are driftwm-core's. The mouse_binding command looks a physical chord, a button or scroll source and a context up through upstream's ContextBindings lookup, and the shell asks it on every press and scroll and maps move, cluster move, pan, zoom and action bindings onto its gestures. A wheel-up or wheel-down binding is answered by a wheel-notch lookup of its own (wheel_up, wheel_down), which the shell makes first for every event of a discrete wheel, as upstream's notch site stands ahead of its continuous lookup: an action binding runs once per wheel line, ten at most for one event, and anything else falls through to the scroll lookup. Known mismatches: resize bindings need --experimental-native-resize; one wheel line counts as one notch, with no accumulator for a high-resolution wheel; while Shift is held AppKit hands a wheel's vertical lines over as horizontal ones, so the notch is read back from the horizontal axis (a sideways wheel turned under Shift then counts as a notch too, which upstream's does not) and the continuous scroll lookup is left with the horizontal lines (a shift-qualified wheel zoom does nothing, a pan goes sideways), seen on events built in memory and not with a wheel; upstream's grammar has no name for the back and forward buttons. No evidence entry is recorded yet: the controller side is covered by exported-C-ABI/JSON scenarios (crates/desktop/tests/config_flow.rs); the shell side is compiled and reviewed only, and every pointer press, drag and scroll is unrun on a live run. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.contract: Match Config.gestures type, validation, default and native behavior.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E for parameters/defaults, dispatch, errors and lifecycle; verify actual native effects when applicable.
rows.implementation_note: Held in the controller's Config: the three context tables a gesture_begin resolves, upstream's defaults included, with none removing a binding and disable_defaults removing them all; the pointer's own context is tried before anywhere, and a malformed entry is upstream's warning and is skipped. Known mismatches: a physical macOS chord can stand for more than one upstream modifier set, and every such set is tried in combo order; a binding whose action does not run yet resolves and is refused when it fires; the resize bindings are gated; an unbound gesture is not forwarded to the application. No evidence entry is recorded yet: the controller dispatch is covered by exported-C-ABI/JSON scenarios with synthetic event streams (crates/desktop/tests/gesture_flow.rs), and one scripted msg session against the built app on 2026-10-09 loaded a [gestures] override and saw upstream's warnings for malformed entries, leaving no saved evidence; the shell's recogniser has only been fed scripted touch sequences in throwaway programs. No physical trackpad gesture has been performed. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.contract: Match SessionConfig.suspend_on_close type, validation, default and native behavior.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E for parameters/defaults, dispatch, errors and lifecycle; verify actual native effects when applicable.
rows.implementation_note: Read when window_closed reports that a bound window is gone. On: a window with a bundle identifier leaves a stand-in, a detached placeholder that keeps its logical id, world frame and stacking. Off, upstream's default: the window leaves the scene and the focus follows. A [[window_rules]] suspend_on_close that matches the bundle identifier (as app_id) or the title overrides the section, and a close-window or suspend-window mark overrides both. Known mismatches: the marks lapse after upstream's 10 seconds, but measured on the navigation clock the host ticks rather than a wall clock; a window without a bundle identifier never leaves a stand-in; the shell reports a window as closed only when its window number leaves the system window list or its process ends, so a window an application merely hides is not seen as closed; no dialog exclusion. No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios only (crates/desktop/tests/lifecycle_flow.rs); the scripted msg launches of the built app on 2026-10-09 had no Screen Recording access, so no window was bound and none closed. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.contract: Match SessionConfig.restore_windows type, validation, default and native behavior.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E for parameters/defaults, dispatch, errors and lifecycle; verify actual native effects when applicable.
rows.implementation_note: Read at every adoption_complete, which the shell sends after the first read of each discovery pass: at launch and when the canvas reopens. On: a saved slot that no running window took back stays as a dormant stand-in. Off, upstream's default: it is dropped. A slot whose titled window the pass names as still existing off screen keeps waiting either way, and while a config file that exists was refused at launch nothing is dropped or made a stand-in, because the built-in defaults do not speak for the file. Stand-ins are kept either way and slots without a bundle identifier are dropped either way. A [[window_rules]] restore_windows overrides the section and is asked twice, with the title and by application alone, as upstream asks it. Known mismatches: upstream reads the flag at save time to decide whether an open window is recorded and restores what was recorded; here applications outlive the canvas, so every window is always saved as a slot, running windows take their slots back by bundle identifier and title, and the flag decides at launch whether an unmatched slot stays; in a run without Screen Recording access or with --manual no discovery pass completes, the flag is never read and no slot is dropped; an untitled window, or one retitled meanwhile, that is off screen during the pass counts as unmatched. No evidence entry is recorded yet: automated coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios only (crates/desktop/tests/lifecycle_flow.rs); the scripted msg launches of the built app on 2026-10-09 had no Screen Recording access, adoption_complete was never sent, and the flag made no observable difference there. Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.contract: Match SessionConfig.restore_camera type, validation, default and native behavior.
rows.acceptance: Define source-matching production-path E2E for parameters/defaults, dispatch, errors and lifecycle; verify actual native effects when applicable.
rows.implementation_note: Read at the first load_config of a run. Off, upstream's default: an output that connects starts at a new output's camera instead of the one saved in the scene file. On: the saved camera is restored. Cameras are always saved, and an output this session has already shown keeps its camera across a disconnect. Known mismatches: a new output's camera puts the world origin at its top-left corner, where upstream centres it; the scene file stands in for upstream's session store. No evidence entry is recorded yet: coverage is exported-C-ABI/JSON controller scenarios only (crates/desktop/tests/config_flow.rs). Native verification and full-row acceptance remain incomplete.

rows.implementation_note: Read at the first load_config of a run. On: the scene file's bookmark registry is laid over the config seeds, a saved value winning per name, and runtime edits are saved. Off, upstream's default: the registry starts from the config seeds alone, runtime edits last until quit, and a save carries the file's registry forward untouched. Known mismatches: the scene file stands in for upstream's session store.
